statements.claim: Rukmi had sworn before his father Bhishmaka and before all the assembled kings that he would not re-enter Kundina until he had slain Krishna and brought his sister back.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116: 'promised before Bhishmaka saying I shall not return to the city of Kundina without slaying Krishna and bringing back Rukshmini'; BP 10.54.17-18: vow made 'in the hearing of all kings' (śṛṇvatāṁ sarva-bhūbhujām).

statements.claim: The whole assembly of svayamvara kings took the road after Krishna — allies of Jarasandha, kings of the Deccan, princes of every house that had hoped to claim the princess of Vidarbha.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.1-8: Krishna's host routed the pursuing kings; HV 1.116: Deccan kings and other mighty car-warriors followed Rukmi in pursuit, and Balarama's Vrishnis 'vanquished Jarāsandha and others'.

statements.claim: Shishupala of Chedi rode up burning with rage, and Krishna told him to put aside his grief; Shishupala answered 'I have been defeated by you seventeen times in battle, and I have never grieved, and never rejoiced.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.9-13: śiśupālaṁ samabhyetya hṛta-dāram ivāturam... 'śaureḥ sapta-daśāhaṁ vai saṁyugāni parājitaḥ / tathāpy ahaṁ na śocāmi na prahṛṣyāmi karhicit'.

statements.claim: Krishna shattered every weapon Rukmi raised — the bow, mace, spear, javelin and shield — and wrecked his chariot, so Rukmi leapt down sword in hand.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.27-30: Acyuta cut the bow, then parigha, paṭṭiśa, śūla, carma-asi, śakti and tomara, and Rukmi leapt from the chariot sword in hand (khaḍga-pāṇir jighāṁsayā); HV 1.116: Krishna 'cut off his bow and car' and Rukmi jumped down with sword and shield.

statements.claim: Rukmini threw herself at Krishna's feet, begging for her brother's life: 'He is my only brother... Give me my brother in charity.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.31: dṛṣṭvā bhrātṛ-vadhodyogaṁ rukmiṇī bhaya-vihvalā; HV 1.116: 'Beholding her brother lying down motionless on earth, Rukshmini, for his life, fell at Vishnu's feet'; VP 5.26: 'He is my only brother... give me my brother in charity.'

statements.claim: Krishna spared Rukmi but bound him, shaved his head and beard, and disfigured him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.34: 'cailena baddhvā tam asādhu-kārīṇaṁ sa-śmaśru-keśaṁ pravapan vyarūpayat' — binding the wicked one, shaving beard and hair, he disfigured him.

statements.claim: Krishna lifted Rukmini up, held and comforted her, and promised her brother his life and safety; Rukmi lay senseless and was carried off the field by his own men.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116: Keshava 'took up her, embraced and consoled her. And then promising safety to Rukshmi he set out'; Rukmi 'fell down unconscious'; Shrutarva 'placed Rukshmi on his own car and took him to his own city'.

statements.claim: Rukmi could not go home; he built a new city in Vidarbha named Bhojakata and ruled the southern districts, while Bhishmaka remained in Kundina.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116: 'seeing his promise broken the haughty and sensitive Rukshmi did not like to enter into the city of Kundina. For his residence he built another city in the province of Bidharbha... under the name of Bhojakata... govern the southern districts... Bhishmaka lived in the city of Kundina.'

statements.claim: Balarama and the Vrishni army, having scattered Jarasandha and the rest, turned for Dwaraka.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116: 'having vanquished Jarāsandha and others, the Vrishnis, headed by Rāma, gladly set out for Dwarka.'

notes: All battle claims map to BP 10.54.1-35 (primary, conf 5) with HV 1.116/VP 5.26 corroboration. Minor variant: HV sets the duel near the Narmada with Rukmi accompanied by an army, while the story follows BP's 'alone' pursuit — flagged in the pack's own variant_notes. Poetic color (dust-wall, 'learned to lose', scattered banners) is connective narration.

statements.claim: Rukmi never returned to Kundina; he built a new capital, Bhojakata, in Vidarbha and ruled the southern districts, while Bhishmaka stayed in Kundina.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116 (passage in pack): 'did not like to enter into the city of Kundina... built another city in the province of Bidharbha... under the name of Bhojakata... govern the southern districts'; 'Bhishmaka lived in the city of Kundina'.

statements.claim: The Yadava host came home to Dwaraka, Balarama at its head after settling with Jarasandha and the pursuing kings.
statements.evidence: HV 1.116: 'having vanquished Jarāsandha and others, the Vrishnis, headed by Rāma, gladly set out for Dwarka.'

statements.claim: Krishna wed Rukmini in due form with the full rites, and she became his queen.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.35-59 rendering: 'Krishna brought Rukmini to Dvaraka and wed her with full rites'; HV 1.116: 'the powerful Keshavā duly espoused Rukshmini'; VP 5.26: 'married Rukminí in due form, having first made her his own by the Rákshasa ritual'.

statements.claim: Dwaraka gave itself to festival: every house celebrated; streets sprinkled with water; doorways hung with mango-leaf garlands, flowers, gems and toranas; auspicious pots at thresholds; incense and lamps; Indra's banners over the gates; conches, drums and singing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.53-56: 'mahotsavo nṝṇāṁ yadu-puryāṁ gṛhe gṛhe', 'pramṛṣṭa-maṇi-kuṇḍalāḥ', 'uttambhitendra-ketubhir vicitra-mālyāmbara-ratna-toraṇaiḥ', 'āpūrṇa-kumbhāguru-dhūpa-dīpakaiḥ', 'sikta-mārgāḥ' — festival in every house, jeweled earrings, Indra banners, garlands/gems/toranas at each gate, filled pots, incense and lamps, sprinkled roads.

statements.claim: Guests came from the Kuru, Srijaya and Kaikeya lands, from Vidarbha and the Yadu and Kunti houses.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.57: 'kuru-sṛñjaya-kaikeya-vidarbha-yadu-kuntayaḥ'.

statements.claim: The story of Rukmini's abduction was sung everywhere in Dwaraka, and great joy filled the city.
statements.evidence: BP 10.54.58-59: 'rukmiṇyā haraṇaṁ śrutvā gīyamānaṁ tatas tataḥ', 'dvārakāyām abhūd rājan mahā-modaḥ puraukasām'.

statements.claim: The Vishnu Purana says Rukmini bore Krishna a son, Pradyumna, a portion of the god of love, who grew into one of the Yadus' greatest warriors; the Harivamsha names her Krishna's first wife.
statements.evidence: VP 5.26 excerpt: 'She bore him the gallant Pradyumna, a portion of the deity of love'; HV 1.116: Rukmini 'was the first wife of Krishna', mother of Pradyumna and ten warrior sons (dreadful in battle, masters of weapons).

statements.claim: Rukmini, who had chosen him before she ever saw him, had staked everything on him.
statements.evidence: Recap of the corpus-chain abduction story (DKS_0200: Rukmini chose Krishna by report and sent a brahmin before meeting him); the emotional framing ('staked everything') is narrative, not a discrete sourceable fact in 10.54.35-59.

notes: The festival passage is almost verbatim-supported by BP 10.54.53-56 (conf 5). 'Before the fire and the witnesses of the Yadu court' is standard-rite connective detail consistent with 'wed her with full rites'. The closing 'Rukmi's exile is his own work' reading is the story's moral gloss, not a factual claim.

statements.claim: Krishna, guest at Indraprastha, went hunting with Arjuna in the great forest, riding Arjuna's monkey-bannered chariot.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.12-13: 'ekadā ratham āruhya vijayo vānara-dhvajam / sākaṁ kṛṣṇena sannaddho vihartuṁ vipinaṁ mahat'; 10.58.25-26 (Maya, rescued from the fire, giving the assembly hall) anchors the Indraprastha setting.

statements.claim: Tigers, wild boars, buffaloes and antelope fell to their arrows, and servants carried the kill to the king for the coming festival day.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.14-15: 'tatrāvidhyac charair vyāghrān śūkarān mahiṣān rurūn / tān ninyuḥ kiṅkarā rājñe medhyān parvaṇy upāgate'.

statements.claim: The two friends bathed in and drank the clear water of the Yamuna and rested on its bank, where they saw a maiden.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.16-17: 'tatropaspṛśya viśadaṁ pītvā vāri mahā-rathau / tām āsādya varārohāṁ su-dvijāṁ rucirānanām'.

statements.claim: Krishna sent Arjuna to ask the maiden her name, her family, and what she hoped for.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.18: 'kā tvaṁ kasyāsi su-śroṇi kuto vā kiṁ cikīrṣasi'; pack rendering: 'Arjuna, sent by Krishna, asked the beautiful maiden her name'.

statements.claim: 'I am Kalindi,' she said, 'daughter of the Sun, and I live in the waters of the Yamuna. I will take no husband but him in whom all beauty dwells.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.20-21: 'nānyaṁ patiṁ vṛṇe vīra tam ṛte śrī-niketanam / kālindīti samākhyātā vasāmi yamunā-jale'; pack excerpt confirms she is daughter of Surya doing penance to win Vishnu as husband.

statements.claim: Her penance and waiting in the river had been for Vishnu himself — for Krishna.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (10.58.12-28): 'she said I am Kalindi, daughter of Surya, doing penance to win Vishnu as husband'.

statements.claim: Krishna took her onto his chariot and in time married her at an auspicious hour when season and stars were favorable.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.27-28: 'sa tena samanujñātaḥ suhṛdbhiś cānumoditaḥ / athopayeme kālindīṁ su-puṇya-rtv-ṛkṣa ūrjite' — married at an auspicious season and constellation; pack rendering: 'Krishna took her on his chariot and later wed her at an auspicious time'.

statements.claim: The marriage was quiet and complete — no armies, no svayamvara, no chase, no envoys.
statements.evidence: Negative framing consistent with the brief BP account (meeting by the water, question, vow, later wedding at an auspicious time); the enumeration of what did NOT happen is connective narration.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.58.12-28 (conf 5). The Indraprastha framing matches the passage's own Maya/assembly-hall context (vv. 25-26). 'Years of waiting', 'stillness of someone who had been waiting' are atmosphere.

statements.claim: In Avanti, the princes Vinda and Anuvinda were long devoted to Duryodhana, and their sister Mitravinda — daughter of Krishna's own aunt — was to be given in svayamvara.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.29-30: 'vindyānuvindyāv āvantyau duryodhana-vaśānugau / rājādhidevyās tanayāṁ mitravindāṁ pitṛ-ṣvasuḥ'; index summary: Krishna 'carries off Mitravinda of Avanti from her svayamvara'.

statements.claim: Before the assembled kings could decide anything, Krishna carried Mitravinda off forcibly and set her in his chariot.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP 10.58.29-55, conf 5): 'Krishna forcibly carried off Mitravinda, the princess of Avanti, before the assembled kings'.

statements.claim: In Kosala, King Nagnajit, a righteous king, had a daughter Satya whom no man could win without subduing seven fierce, untamable bulls that had broken every suitor.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.31-32, 42: 'nagnajin nāma kauśalya āsīd rājāti-dhārmikaḥ / na tāṁ śekur nṛpā voḍhum ajitvā sapta-go-vṛṣān'; 'saptaite go-vṛṣā vīra durdāntā duravagrahāḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna went to Kosala; Nagnajit rose from his seat and received him with honor, and Satya, seeing him, chose him in her heart.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.33-35: 'tāṁ śrutvā vṛṣa-jil-labhyāṁ bhagavān sātvatāṁ patiḥ / sa kośala-patiḥ prītaḥ pratyutthānāsanādibhiḥ'; 'varaṁ vilokyābhimataṁ samāgataṁ narendra-kanyā cakame ramā-patim'.

statements.claim: Nagnajit said the agreement had been made before all the world: 'These seven bulls are fierce, and beyond control. Subdue them, and my daughter is yours.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.41-43: 'kintv asmābhiḥ kṛtaḥ pūrvaṁ samayaḥ... saptaite go-vṛṣā vīra durdāntā duravagrahāḥ / yad ime nigṛhītāḥ syus tvayaiva yadu-nandana'.

statements.claim: Krishna bound up his garment and seemed to be everywhere at once, as if seven Krishnas stood in the pen; he roped all seven bulls, their pride broken.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.44-45: 'baddhvā parikaraṁ prabhuḥ / baddhvā tān dāmabhiḥ śaurir bhagna-darpān hataujasaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'he multiplied himself sevenfold and with ease subdued seven untamable bulls'.

statements.claim: The amazed king of Kosala gave Krishna his daughter; queens rejoiced, conches and kettledrums sounded, and brahmin blessings rose.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.46-48: 'tataḥ prītaḥ sutāṁ rājā dadau kṛṣṇāya vismitaḥ / rāja-patnyaś ca duhituḥ kṛṣṇaṁ labdhvā priyaṁ patim / śaṅkha-bhery-ānakā nedur gīta-vādya-dvijāśiṣaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna gave in return ten thousand cows, nine thousand elephants and chariots in plenty, placed Satya on his chariot, and set out for Dwaraka with a great army.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.49-51: 'daśa-dhenu-sahasrāṇi pāribarham adād vibhuḥ / nava-nāga-sahasrāṇi nāgāc chata-guṇān rathān / dampatī ratham āropya mahatyā senayā vṛtau'.

statements.claim: The losing kings raised a cry and loosed volleys of arrows at the chariot, and Arjuna, riding with Krishna, turned every shaft aside.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.52-53: 'śrutvaitad rurudhur bhūpā nayantaṁ pathi kanyakām / tān asyataḥ śara-vrātān bandhu-priya-kṛd arjunaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna came home to Dwaraka with two new brides: Mitravinda, carried off from Avanti, and Satya, won in the bull-pen of Kosala.
statements.evidence: Index summary and pack excerpt (BP 10.58.29-55): both episodes narrated as one journey, per the pack's variant note that the Bhagavata presents them together.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.58.29-55 (conf 5). The 'shouting after a departing chariot' and 'Avanti learned its gates were no shield' are connective color. Story's framing of one journey matches the BP sequence and the pack's variant note.

statements.claim: In the inner chamber, Krishna lay on a couch white as milk foam, and Rukmini fanned him with a jewel-handled fan she had taken from a friend's hand; the air carried the scent of parijata and bees moved through mallika garlands.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.3-6: 'mallikā-dāmabhiḥ puṣpair dvirepha-kula-nādite / pārijāta-vanāmoda-vāyunā... payaḥ-phena-nibhe śubhre paryaṅke... vāla-vyajanam ādāya ratna-daṇḍaṁ sakhī-karāt'.

statements.claim: Krishna said great kings had sought her — Shishupala, Shalva, Jarasandha, Dantavakra — and asked whom she had chosen: a man with nothing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.10-17: 'tān prāptān arthino hitvā caidyādīn smara-durmadān... caidya-śālva-jarāsandha-dantavakrādayo nṛpāḥ'; 'niṣkiñcanā vayaṁ śaśvan niṣkiñcana-jana-priyāḥ'.

statements.claim: He said the penniless were the only people he could call his own, and he kept company with folk who walked hidden roads the world never saw.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.12-13: 'aspaṣṭa-vartmanāṁ puṁsām aloka-patham īyuṣām / niṣkiñcanā vayaṁ śaśvan niṣkiñcana-jana-priyāḥ'.

statements.claim: He said he was not the sort to run after wives, sons and household splendor, and urged her to choose a worthy kshatriya, a bull among kings.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.16, 19: 'athātmano 'nurūpaṁ vai bhajasva kṣatriyarṣabham'; 'udāsīnā vayaṁ nūnaṁ na stry-apatyārtha-kāmukāḥ'.

statements.claim: From the lips of the lord of the three worlds Rukmini had never heard an unkind word before that day; she heard this one as a sentence.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.21: 'iti trilokeśa-pates tadātmanas priyasya devy aśruta-pūrvam apriyam' — the queen heard from the lord of the three worlds an unkindness never heard before.

statements.claim: Her eyes filled with tears dark with collyrium, she traced the floor with her toe, the jeweled fan slipped from her hand, and she fainted outright, her hair scattering like a plantain tree struck by wind.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.22-23: 'padā su-jātena nakhāruṇa-śrīyā bhuvaṁ likhanty aśrubhir añjanāsitaiḥ... hastāc chlathad-valayato vyajanaṁ papāta... rambheva vāyu-vihato pravikīrya keśān' — writing on the ground with tears of collyrium, the fan falling, fainting like a plantain tree struck by wind with hair scattered.

statements.claim: Krishna rose from the couch, lifted her in his arms, wiped the tears from her eyes and began to comfort her, the game over for him in that instant.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.24-27: 'paryaṅkād avaruhyāśu tām utthāpya catur-bhujaḥ / pramṛjyāśru-kale netre stanau copahatau śucā / sāntvayām āsa sāntva-jñaḥ kṛpayā kṛpaṇāṁ prabhuḥ'.

statements.claim: He meant it as play — a jest, a game of teasing — and his smile was real.
statements.evidence: The jest is confirmed as playful in the paired episode (BP 10.60.28-30, 'I spoke in jest'); the characterization of his inward intent and 'real smile' is interpretive connective narration.

statements.claim: Rukmini had chosen him across the ruin of her own life — sending him word against her brother's wishes, climbing into his chariot at her svayamvara while the kings looked on — and every king he named had been gathered in that hall.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.10: the named kings 'came as suitors' (prāptān arthino... caidyādīn); her svayamvara choice and brother's opposition are the corpus-chain events (DKS_0199-0200, BP 10.52-53), and Rukmini's own speech in the paired episode confirms the messenger plot (BP 10.60.54-56).

notes: Nearly every sensory and emotional beat maps directly to BP 10.60.1-27 (conf 5), including the plantain-tree simile, collyrium tears, and fan falling from her hand. The 'jest wrapped in love' analysis is narrative commentary, not a factual claim.

statements.claim: Waking in Krishna's arms, she heard him say he had spoken in jest — he had wanted to see her face trembling between love and anger, the supreme gain of a householder, which no treasure could equal.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.29-30: 'mukhaṁ ca prema-saṁrambha-sphuritādharam īkṣitum / ayaṁ hi paramo lābho gṛheṣu gṛha-medhinām'; pack excerpt: Krishna said 'I spoke in jest to hear your words'.

statements.claim: Rukmini named kings — Anga and Vainya, Jayanta, Nahusha and Gaya — who held the whole earth and, wanting only him, laid their kingdoms down and walked into the forest.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.40: 'yad-vāñchayā nṛpa-śikhāmaṇayo 'ṅga-vainya-jāyanta-nāhuṣa-gayādaya aikya-patyam / rājyaṁ visṛjya viviśur vanam ambujākṣa'.

statements.claim: The guardians of the worlds carried tribute to his feet, and sages who had laid aside punishment worshipped him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.36, 38: 'yasmai baliṁ bali-bhujo 'pi haranty ajādyāḥ'; 'tvaṁ nyasta-daṇḍa-munibhir gaditānubhāva'.

statements.claim: At her svayamvara his bow had spoken once and the kings scattered like animals before a lion; he carried her off the way a lion carries off its share.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.39: 'bhūpān vidrāvya śārṅga-ninadena jahartha māṁ tvam / siṁho yathā sva-balim īśa paśūn'.

statements.claim: Having breathed the fragrance of his lotus feet — the fragrance that releases the sorrowful — no woman would choose any other refuge.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.41: 'kānyaṁ śrayeta tava pāda-saroja-gandham āghrāya san-mukharitaṁ janatāpavargam'.

statements.claim: She would rather be a servant in the house of even one of his devotees than any queen; a woman who does not love his feet is a living corpse, skin and bone dressed in finery.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.43-44: kings become servants in the houses where his stories are sung; 'jīvac-chavaṁ bhajati kānta-matir vimūḍhā yā te padābja-makarandam ajighratī strī' — a woman not savoring his lotus-feet honey is a living corpse; and her love should stand 'in this world and the next' (10.60.45).

statements.claim: She did not hold his words false: a wanton's heart runs after every new thing, but hers, once given, did not wander.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.46-47: 'naivālīkam ahaṁ manye vacas te madhusūdana / vyūḍhāyāś cāpi puṁścalyā mano 'bhyeti navaṁ navam'.

statements.claim: Krishna praised her faithfulness: at her own wedding she had ignored the gathered kings and sent a brahmin to him in secret; she had never complained of her brother's enmity for fear of wounding him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.54-55: 'sva-vivāha-kāle prāptān nṛpān na vigaṇayya raho-haro me prasthāpito dvijaḥ'; 'bhrātur virūpa-karaṇaṁ yudhi nirjitasya... duḥkhaṁ samuttham asaho 'smad-ayoga-bhītyā naivābravīḥ kim api'.

statements.claim: Those who seek him only for the gifts of marriage are poor in fortune even when rich; her devotion was of the kind that frees a soul from the world.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.52-53: 'māṁ prāpya māniny apavarga-sampadaṁ vāñchanti ye sampada eva tat-patim / te manda-bhāgā niraye 'pi ye nṛṇām'; 'mayi tvayā kṛtānuvṛttir bhava-mocanī'.

statements.claim: As Krishna lived with Rukmini, so he dwelt in the homes of his other wives — the Lord of the universe, in each house simply a husband at home.
statements.evidence: BP 10.60.58: 'tathānyāsām api vibhur gṛheṣu gṛhavān iva'.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.60.28-58 (conf 5); Krishna's reference to Rukmi's death 'at the dice-gathering' (10.60.55) is a source-internal chronology note, not an error in this story. The closing peace imagery is connective.

statements.claim: The wedding of Aniruddha, Krishna's grandson, to Rukmi's granddaughter was held in peace in Rukmi's city of Bhojakata, Rukmi having swallowed his old enmity with Krishna.
statements.evidence: HV 1.118: Aniruddha, son of Pradyumna (Keshava's son), wed Rukshmavati, Rukmi's granddaughter, celebrated with great festivity; 'Rukshmi used always to show rivalry with Krishna; still... he cast off his enmity'.

statements.claim: After the ceremony, the Kalinga king and the gathered kings — the king of Ashmaka, Rukmi's son Shrutarva, Chanura, Kratha, Anshuman, Jayatsena and Deccan princes — urged Rukmi, an expert at dice, to play against Balarama, who loved the game though he played it like a cowherd.
statements.evidence: HV 1.118: 'the liberal king of Ashmaka, Venudāri, Rukshma's son Shrutarvā, Chānura, Krātha, Angshuman, the highly powerful king of Kalinga, Jayatsena... chiefs of Deccan spoke secretly to Rukshmi: You are an expert in dice...'; BP 10.61.26-27: 'kāliṅga-pramukhā nṛpāḥ... anakṣa-jño hy ayaṁ rājann api tad-vyasanaṁ mahat'.

statements.claim: The hall had golden pillars, a flower-strewn floor sprinkled with sandal water, and golden seats.
statements.evidence: HV 1.118: 'entered into a beautiful hall with golden pillars and its floor covered with flowers. And it was sprinkled with sandal water... sat upon golden seats.'

statements.claim: Rama joined gladly, saying he was only sporting; the wagers climbed from a hundred coins to a thousand to ten thousand, until Rukmi set a stake of a hundred thousand and Rama matched it and lost, his anger rising like the sea at high tide.
statements.evidence: HV 1.118: Rāma gladly said 'See I am sporting'; betted from ten to a thousand gold coins and was repeatedly defeated. BP 10.61.28-30: 'śataṁ sahasram ayutaṁ rāmas tatrādade paṇam / tato lakṣaṁ rukmy agṛhṇād glahaṁ tatrājayad balaḥ / manyunā kṣubhitaḥ śrīmān samudra iva parvaṇi'.

statements.claim: Mastering his wrath, Rama calmly offered one final wager of everything on a single throw; this time, though Rukmi cheated, Rama won — the game was fair.
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.31: 'taṁ cāpi jitavān rāmo dharmeṇa chalam āśritaḥ' — Rama won that too by righteousness though (Rukmi) resorted to fraud; HV 1.118: 'although a master of anger... controlling his passions, calmly said: My next bet is one hundred koti' and Rukshmi was 'rightly defeated by Rāma'.

statements.claim: A voice from the sky declared the stake had been won by Balarama and by Balarama alone.
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.32: 'tadābravīn nabho-vāṇī balenaiva jito glahaḥ'; VP 5.28 (pack excerpt note) and pack rendering confirm the heavenly voice.

statements.claim: Rukmi, urged on by the kings, refused to hear it and jeered: 'Cowherds who live in the forest know nothing of dice.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.33-34: 'tām anādṛtya vaidarbho duṣṭa-rājanya-coditaḥ / naivākṣa-kovidā yūyaṁ gopālā vana-gocarāḥ'.

statements.claim: The Kalinga king laughed loudest, showing every tooth; Balarama seized him, dashed him to the floor and struck the teeth out of his head.
statements.evidence: HV 1.118: 'Hearing it the king of Kalinga, delightedly and showing his teeth, laughed aloud'; 'he struck down the teeth of the Kalinga king'; BP 10.61.36: 'kaliṅga-rājaṁ tarasā gṛhītvā daśame pade'.

statements.claim: The kings who had mocked him he broke where they stood — arms, thighs, skulls — until the flower-strewn hall ran red.
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.37: 'anye nirbhinna-bāhūru-śiraso rudhirokṣitāḥ' — others with broken arms, thighs and heads, drenched in blood.

statements.claim: Rukmi he struck down dead with his iron club; Krishna said nothing, good or ill, because the dead man was Rukmini's brother.
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.38: 'nihate rukmiṇi śyāle nābravīt sādhv asādhu vā'; pack rendering: 'Balarama struck him down with his club, and Krishna said nothing, fearing to wound Rukmini'; weapon variant (club vs dice-board) noted in pack variant_notes (HV/VP).

statements.claim: The wedding party placed Aniruddha and his bride in the finest chariot and left for Dwaraka that night.
statements.evidence: BP 10.61.39: 'tato 'niruddhaṁ saha sūryayā varaṁ rathaṁ samāropya yayuḥ kuśasthalīm' — placing Aniruddha with his bride on a fine chariot, they went to Kusasthali (Dwaraka).

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.61.26-39 (conf 5) with HV 1.118 corroboration. 'Same night' is connective timing (BP does not specify). Story's earlier wager ladder follows BP (100/1000/10000, then a lakh); HV uses different figures (10→1000, then a koti) — a source-number variant the pack itself preserves, not an error.

statements.claim: Years afterward, when Draupadi asked Krishna's queens how each had come to marry him, Lakshmana answered with a story about a fish.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.16-38 (pack): 'Asked by Draupadi how Krishna married them, Lakshmana recounts that her father arranged a svayamvara with a fish target'; 10.83.17 'śrī-lakṣmaṇovāca'.

statements.claim: On the way, Krishna had married Bhadra, daughter of his aunt Srutakirti, given to him by her brothers.
statements.evidence: BP 10.58.55: 'śrutakīrteḥ sutāṁ bhadrāṁ upayeme pitṛ-ṣvasuḥ'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna wed Bhadra, daughter of his aunt Srutakirti, given by her brothers'.

statements.claim: In Madra, the king proclaimed a svayamvara for his daughter Lakshmana with a fish target that no archer could see directly, only its reflection in the water below; the king who strung the bow and pierced the fish would win her.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.17-18, 23: 'matsyaḥ pārthepsayā kṛtaḥ'; 'matsyābhāsaṁ jale vīkṣya jñātvā ca tad-avasthitim' — the fish's semblance seen in the water; 10.58.56: Lakshmana, daughter of the king of Madra.

statements.claim: The kings of the earth came; some could not string the bow at all, and the kings of Magadha, Ambashta and Cedi, the strongest, strung it but every arrow they loosed at the reflection missed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.21-23: 'ādāya vyasṛjan kecit sajyaṁ kartum anīśvarāḥ / sajyaṁ kṛtvāpare vīrā māgadhāmbaṣṭha-cedipāḥ / matsyābhāsaṁ jale vīkṣya jñātvā ca tad-avasthitim'.

statements.claim: Krishna took up the bow, which bent in his hands, glanced once at the fish in the water, and with a single arrow brought the fish down; celestial drums and shouts of victory sounded from the sky and earth.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.24-26: 'rājanyeṣu nivṛtteṣu bhagna-māneṣu māniṣu / tasmin sandhāya viśikhaṁ matsyaṁ vīkṣya sakṛj jale / divi dundubhayo nedur jaya-śabda-yutā bhuvi'.

statements.claim: Lakshmana entered the arena with chiming anklets, holding a garland of golden-gleaming jewels and a shy smile, and set the garland on Krishna's shoulder; conches, drums and bheris answered.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.27-29: 'tad raṅgam āviśam ahaṁ kala-nūpurābhyāṁ padbhyāṁ pragṛhya kanakojvala-ratna-mālām... sa-vrīḍa-hāsa-vadanā... aṁse 'nurakta-hṛdayā nidadhe sva-mālām'; 'mṛdaṅga-paṭahāḥ śaṅkha-bhery-ānakādayaḥ'.

statements.claim: As the old verse puts it, he carried off the fair daughter of Madra the way Garuda seizes nectar from the gods.
statements.evidence: Pack tradition note and BP 10.58.56 rendering: 'he carried off Lakshmana, the fair daughter of the king of Madra, from her svayamvara like Garuda seizing nectar'.

statements.claim: The losing kings surged to stop him on the road; Daruka lifted Lakshmana into the chariot drawn by four fine horses, and Krishna cut down arms, legs and necks with arrows from Sharnga until the road lay open.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.30-34: 'māṁ tāvad ratham āropya haya-ratna-catuṣṭayam / dārukaś codayām āsa kāñcanopaskaraṁ ratham / te 'nvasajjanta rājanyā niṣeddhuṁ pathi kecana / te śārṅga-cyuta-bāṇaughaiḥ kṛtta-bāhv-aṅghri-kandharāḥ'.

statements.claim: He entered Dwaraka like the sun entering its home, through gates hung with banners; and the king of Madra honored the guests Krishna had left behind with serving women, wealth, elephants, chariots and horses.
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.35-37: 'samāviśat taraṇir iva sva-ketanam' (entered like the sun its own abode); 'pitā me pūjayām āsa suhṛt-sambandhi-bāndhavān / dāsībhiḥ sarva-sampadbhir bhaṭebha-ratha-vājibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: Lakshmana ended her story: 'We are only servants in the home of that self-satisfied Lord.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.83.38: 'ātmārāmasya tasyemā vayaṁ vai gṛha-dāsikāḥ' — we are verily the house-servants of that self-delighting (ātmārāma) Lord.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.58.55-57 + 10.83.16-38 (both conf 5). 'A marriage of kinsmen, arranged and blessed' glosses Bhadra's account per the pack. Closing reflection on Lakshmana's words is connective commentary.
